full_text:
Cyclone Murasu is expected to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast around midnight on November 2, bringing heavy to extremely heavy rainfall to several districts on Tuesday, November 3.
According to the India Meteorological Department's (IMD) latest bulletin issued on November 2, the severe cyclonic storm was centred about 160 km east-southeast of Nellore at 8.30 am.
The cyclone is likely to cross the coast between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, between 11.30 pm on November 2 and 4 am on November 3, with winds of 100–110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph.
The latest forecast has also revised the district-wise rainfall warnings for November 3.
According to the IMD's November 2 bulletin, the following warnings apply for November 3:
Red alert — Extremely heavy rainfall: Palnadu, Nandyal and Tirupati.
Orange alert — Heavy to very heavy rainfall: Eluru, NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, SPSR Nellore, Kurnool, YSR Kadapa, Annamayya and Chittoor.
Yellow alert — Heavy rainfall: Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli, Kakinada, East Godavari, Konaseema, West Godavari, Anantapuramu and Sri Sathya Sai.
The warnings indicate the possibility of rainfall of varying intensity at isolated locations within these districts.
The IMD has forecast widespread light to moderate rainfall or thundershowers across coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on November 3, with rainfall also likely at many places in Rayalaseema.
Schools in NTR and Eluru districts were closed on Monday, November 2, as a precautionary measure amid the cyclone warning.
With the IMD forecasting heavy rainfall and strong winds on November 3, school operations and transport services could face disruptions, particularly in districts under red and orange alerts.
However, no statewide school holiday for November 3 has been established by the weather bulletin.
Any decision to close schools will be taken by the respective district Collectors or education authorities based on local weather conditions and safety assessments.
Parents and students should monitor official district administration announcements for confirmed school holiday information.
The IMD has also forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 4, although the overall intensity of rainfall and winds is expected to reduce.

Visakhapatnam: The deep depression over the southwest Bay of Bengal intensified into a cyclonic storm ‘Murasu’ on Sunday and is expected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur from Monday midnight to the early hours of Tuesday, the IMD has predicted.
Days after AP was battered by ‘very severe’ cyclonic storm Arnab, the state is now bracing for another spell of high-speed winds and heavy rainfall, with the govt stepping up preparedness across the coastal and Rayalaseema regions.
Cyclone Murasu is likely to cross the south AP coast as a severe cyclonic storm on Monday, packing sustained winds of 100kmph to 110kmph and gusts of up to 120kmph. It is likely to trigger heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in parts of coastal AP and Rayalaseema on Monday and Tuesday.
Murasu, a name given by India, which means ‘drum’ in Tamil, will mark a rare instance of a tropical cyclone over North Indian Ocean. It refers to an ancient percussion instrument used to disseminate information and alert people about natural disasters.
The new weather system over the southwest and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal moved west-northwestward at 25kmph in the past six hours and lay centred about 420km east-southeast of Chennai, 490km east-southeast of Nellore, 500km southeast of Machilipatnam, 510km east-southeast of Kavali, 530km southeast of Ongole, and 560km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam.
As cyclone Murasu heads toward the AP coast, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall on Monday in five districts — Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam and Nellore. Extremely heavy rainfall is likely to disrupt normal life in these areas.
IMD has also issued an orange alert for heavy to very heavy rainfall on Monday in seven districts — East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, NTR, Palnadu, Tirupati and Chittoor. A yellow alert for heavy rainfall has been issued for ASR, Kakinada, Konaseema, Nandyal, Kadapa and Annamayya districts.
For Tuesday, IMD has issued a red alert for ASR, Eluru and NTR districts, and an orange alert for Chittoor, Annamayya, Tirupati, Nellore, Prakasam, Palnadu and Vizianagaram districts.
Heavy rainfall is also likely in parts of Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Anakapalle, Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Kadapa, Nandyal, Kurnool, Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai districts on Tuesday. On Wednesday, parts of Nellore, Prakasam, Bapatla, Guntur and Krishna districts are likely to receive heavy rainfall.
